c.tagline: A 15th-century castle rising mid-lake, sopranos singing from its ramparts every July, and 14,000 islands waiting in the mist beyond.

card: Finland is one of the most cashless countries in Europe — contactless Visa/Mastercard/mobile pay is accepted everywhere, from hotels and restaurants to market stalls and sauna kiosks; carrying cash is rarely necessary.

taxi.color: White cars with a yellow 'TAKSI' roof sign — standard Finnish taxi livery
taxi.fareNote: Fixed-price app quotes are common; expect surcharges on nights, weekends and during the July Opera Festival when demand spikes

emergency.note: 112 is Finland's single number for all emergencies (police, fire, ambulance); English-speaking operators are available and the free 112 Suomi app can share your GPS location

english.label: Easy to get by in English

walk: Highly walkable core — the rail station, Kauppatori market square, Olavinkatu shopping street and Olavinlinna Castle all sit within a 15–20 minute walk of each other, connected by bridges over narrow lake channels; a car or bus is only needed for day trips to Kerimäki or Punkaharju.

safety.safety: Very high — Finland ranks among the safest countries in the world year after year; solo travelers, including women walking alone at night, consistently report feeling secure.
safety.crime: Petty theft and violent crime are both rare. The main real-world hazards are icy sidewalks and low winter light rather than crime.

hood_landmark.Talvisalo: Savonlinna National Urban Park waterfront trails

hood_desc: The compact heart of Savonlinna, packed with shops, cafes, the lakeside Kauppatori market and the pedestrian Olavinkatu — home base for most visitors and the launch point for lake cruises.
The peninsula wrapping around Olavinlinna Castle, alive with opera-goers and cruise passengers in July, otherwise a quiet residential neighborhood with marina views straight onto the fortress.
A green island just off downtown, linked by footbridge, centered on the historic casino-spa complex and Sulosaari nature park — a peaceful escape minutes from the action.
A leafy, mostly residential district within Savonlinna's National Urban Park, laced with waterfront walking paths and early-1900s wooden villas.
A quiet lakeside residential area west of downtown, popular with locals for its swimming beach, forest trails and riding stables.
lodging: Original Sokos Hotel Casino Spa Vuorilinna

water.note: Finnish tap water is excellent and safe everywhere.

transit.sys: No trains, trams or metro within town — local Savonlinja town/regional buses plus a compact walkable core
transit.hours: Local buses run roughly 6:00–19:00 on weekdays with sparse weekend service
transit.pay: Cash or contactless card on board; a Waltti card pays off only for frequent regional bus use
transit.map: Savonlinja/Matkahuolto regional timetables published online — no metro-style transit map exists or is needed
transit.note: Most visitors never ride a bus — downtown, the castle, harbor and market square are all walkable; buses mainly serve outlying districts like Kellarpelto, Nojanmaa and the airport

transport.air: Savonlinna Airport (SVL) offers seasonal flights to Helsinki (about 55 minutes) on small regional carriers, mainly timed around the July Opera Festival; most travelers instead fly into Helsinki-Vantaa (HEL) and continue by train or bus
transport.train: VR runs several daily direct or connecting trains from Helsinki (some changing at Parikkala) in roughly 4–4.5 hours, with fares from about €17–40 one-way
transport.bus: OnniBus and Matkahuolto/Savonlinja coaches connect Helsinki, Turku, Jyväskylä and Kuopio to Savonlinna, with Helsinki taking about 4.5–5.5 hours
transport.ferry: Seasonal lake steamships (S/S Punkaharju, S/S Salama and others) link Savonlinna to Punkaharju and other Saimaa towns from May to September — a scenic experience rather than a primary way to arrive
transport.car: About 335 km / 4 hours from Helsinki via highways 5 and 14; useful for independent day trips to Kerimäki and Punkaharju but unnecessary within town

airport.name: Savonlinna Airport
airport.transport: Airport taxi or pre-booked transfer (no scheduled public bus to the terminal); given SVL's limited seasonal schedule, most travelers fly into Helsinki-Vantaa and connect by a roughly 4-hour train ride instead

net.m: Excellent 4G/5G coverage across town and most of the lake archipelago
net.w: Free wifi is standard in hotels, cafes, the library and the ferry terminal
net.fwn: Nearly every cafe, hotel lobby, and public building offers free wifi, so you're rarely without a signal downtown
net.ap: Not essential thanks to widespread free wifi and EU roaming for European visitors, but a cheap prepaid or eSIM plan from Elisa, Telia or DNA (sold at R-Kioski and supermarkets) is easy to grab for continuous coverage on day trips to Kerimäki or Punkaharju

tip.s: Not expected — service is built into listed prices and wages
tip.r: Rounding up the bill or leaving 5–10% for exceptional service is appreciated but never obligatory
